name: backlog-tracker-rules-tests
description: Tests for backlog-tracker's access-control layer (Firestore security rules, the MCP server's logic, the MCP server over real HTTP driven by the official MCP client SDK), for scripts/ helpers that are easiest to verify against a real disposable git repo (the faq/data/index.json merge-conflict resolver, and the deployment train's lock-recompute logic — pure predicate, the real Cloud Function trigger under stubbed SDKs, and the real branch-archive/reset git logic), and for the FAQ editor's content round-trip in a real browser (opt-in, needs Chromium).

scripts.test: npm run test:mcp && npm run test:client && npm run test:app-boots && npm run test:train-lock && npm run test:skill-history && npm run test:build-batches && npm run test:faq-index && npm run test:rules && npm run test:preview-url && npm run test:preview-url-pin && npm run test:generated-builds
scripts.test:train-lock: node train-lock.test.js && node train-lock-trigger.test.js && node train-lock-branch-archive.test.js && node train-carried.test.js

//: The firebase client version here is independent of the 10.13.2 SDK the app loads from gstatic: this one only drives the emulator, and the rules under test are evaluated server-side. It tracks whatever @firebase/rules-unit-testing peers against.
